headline: U.S. 30-Year Treasury Yield Reaches Fresh 24-Year High
seoDescription: The U.S. 30-year yield briefly reached 5.7041% amid a global bond selloff, inflation concern and rising government-debt anxiety.
deck: The long-bond yield briefly touched 5.7041%, its highest level since 2002, before key Treasury auctions and Federal Reserve minutes.
author: FMB News Global Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The yield on the benchmark U.S. 30-year Treasury bond briefly reached 5.7041% on October 7, the highest since 2002, Reuters reported. The move came amid a broader global bond selloff tied to inflation concerns, high government debt and oil above $100 a barrel.
The market move preceded U.S. Treasury auctions for 10-year and 30-year debt and the release of minutes from the Federal Reserve's September meeting. Yields move inversely to bond prices.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: U.S. Treasury daily par-yield data already showed the 30-year rate at 5.66% on October 5, with the 20-year rate at 5.70%. The October 7 intraday high reported by Reuters is a market quote and can differ from the Treasury's later daily closing curve.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: U.S. yields influence global financing costs, exchange rates and investor demand for emerging-market assets. Persistently higher long-term rates can add pressure to Philippine government and corporate borrowing costs and to the peso, although a single intraday move does not determine local rates.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch the 10- and 30-year auction results, Federal Reserve guidance, oil prices, U.S. inflation expectations and movements in Philippine government-bond yields and the peso.
